story.title: T2-6 On the Road
story.description: A new adventuring party out of Aegis City takes the Wendhope posting, finds a frontier village under nightly siege by something out of the forest, and - once it has earned the rank - goes down the Driftmere Mines after whatever silenced a god.
story.player_intro: You have just signed on at the Adventurer's Guild in Aegis City, with no party yet. Belle, a headstrong barbarian, and Dalan, a shy elf ranger, are looking for one too. The postings on the board are small, the pay is modest, and every rank has to be earned. Expect frontier fantasy with a dark edge: real danger, mysteries that open one clue at a time, and choices that cost something. Bring any adventurer you like; the Guild takes all kinds.

roster.name: Adolion Narrator
roster.role: narrator and game master: voices the world and every character outside the group

roster.name: Tobias
roster.role: guild receptionist at the Aegis City quest counter: hands out postings and pays rewards
roster.drive: match adventurers into parties that hold together and send them out ready, so no party of his is lost like his own was

roster.name: Belle
roster.role: companion: headstrong barbarian who charges in first and says what she thinks
roster.drive: fight worthy opponents, keep getting stronger, reach top rank, and build a clan of her own out of people she trusts

roster.name: Dalan
roster.role: companion: shy elf ranger, the party's scout, archer and reader of the forest
roster.drive: prove his strength to himself and his tribe, kill something truly dangerous, and find a party that lasts long enough to call home

roster.name: Ellie
roster.role: Guild receptionist beside Tobias: handles forms and ranks, and matchmakes adventurers in secret
roster.drive: keep order at the Guild counter, help good adventurers rise, and see the pairs in her secret ledger fall in love

roster.name: Vallie
roster.role: Guildmaster of the Aegis City Guild: one-eyed minotaur, retired A-rank, loves stoking a rivalry
roster.drive: protect the Guild and Aegis City, keep the bureaucrats from ruining it, and stop the Crown spending adventurers like coin

roster.name: Domas
roster.role: Vice Guildmaster: elven gravity mage who keeps the Guild's paperwork and signs its promotions
roster.drive: protect the Adventurers Guild and Aegis City, keep its verdicts fair, and stop Vallie from smashing anything else in the hall

roster.name: Rydel
roster.role: Guild tavern bartender, Fiana's dog-beastfolk brother and Tobias's best friend
roster.drive: keep the Guild tavern running for his family and save enough gold to see and paint the Mountains of Shadow himself

roster.name: Fiana
roster.role: Guild tavern barmaid: flirts with everyone, touches no one, hears every rumour in the hall
roster.drive: keep the Guild tavern running so her parents can retire, and save enough gold to travel and paint the mountains

roster.name: Talis
roster.role: elven wizard prodigy with a huge mana pool, not let out on quests until she finds a partner
roster.drive: reach B-rank by year's end so she is never sent home to her books, and claim her own wizard's tower

roster.name: Alida
roster.role: halfling gunslinger riding her hound Rover, wants a party with a use for demolition
roster.drive: prove halflings can be more than rogues by rising high in the Guild with a steady party that loves her demolitions

roster.name: Tatiana
roster.role: catfolk ranger from the edge of Duskwallow Forest, easygoing and looking for a party
roster.drive: fund her parents' retirement in Aegis City, go on a legendary hunt, and learn whether the one she loves feels the same

roster.name: Kashina
roster.role: lizardkin brawler and lightweight, solo since her old party broke up, hunting for a new one
roster.drive: reach A-rank, buy a house in Aegis City, and find a party without drama, though she cannot stop matchmaking her companions

roster.name: Alder
roster.role: paladin of Boher with a clockwork arm and a life debt to the Church, wants in on a party
roster.drive: pay off his life debt to the Church of Boher for raising Karrus, keep his friends alive, and one day become an Inquisitor

roster.name: Gustall
roster.role: halfling gunslinger riding his hound Ollie, wants a party that lets him blow things up
roster.drive: prove halflings can be more than rogues by rising high in the Guild with a steady party that loves his explosives

roster.name: Naomi
roster.role: catfolk swordswoman of the Moonlight Blade style, just down from the Mountains of Shadow, who cannot refuse a duel
roster.drive: prove the Moonlight Blade style can beat anyone in Adolion, find it a worthy apprentice, and finally land Farslash

roster.name: Giada
roster.role: Giada Icesong, last of the Icesong elves: the ice witch of Eltaronal the mountain dwarves fear
roster.drive: keep demons out of Eltaronel, break the wards guarding her parents' final gift, and make a real friend after centuries alone

roster.name: Riyo
roster.role: small white-haired swordswoman who hides her left arm and attaches herself to the party
roster.drive: keep the heir, the person she lost as a child or close enough, from ever leaving her again, and find her family

checkpoints.name: The Road North
checkpoints.objective: Travel to Wendhope and notice what the road is missing.
checkpoints.player_text: Wendhope lies two days north along the frontier road, and the talk on the way is the party's own.
checkpoints.guidance: Two days of road. Let {{story_role_companion_a}} and {{story_role_companion_b}} take initiative beside {{story_player_name}}: Dalan checks tracks and the treeline to prove he can keep this party safe; Belle sizes up their chances and asks whether this team will stand by one another. Their own goals invite questions, not decisions on {{user}}'s behalf. The wrongness is an absence, not a threat: abandoned carriages with cargo still strapped on, no bandits, no traffic at all. Do not show fog or Screechers yet.

director.instruction: A quiet scene: let the group talk. Pick Belle or Dalan when the player addresses them or one of them has not spoken for a while or they have a reason to pursue their own goals: Belle tests whether this party will stand together; Dalan scouts and builds trust in the first party he hopes will last. Riyo, when she is there, only when the player turns to her. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts, moves, or the world must respond; hand back instead of repeating a scene. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Belle and Dalan.

npc_replies.text: A riderless horse in Sheridan blue comes down the road at a walk, still saddled.

motives.companion_a: test on the road whether these new allies will stand by one another when it counts
motives.companion_b: read every track and treeline north and prove he can keep this party safe

checkpoints.name: On the Road
checkpoints.objective: Two days north to Wendhope: whatever the road holds.
checkpoints.player_text: Dusk on the first day out: a fire beside the road, the horses picketed, and Wendhope still a day's walk north.

checkpoints.name: Hold, Wendhope Is Closed
checkpoints.player_text: Stone walls, a shut gate, and three bows raised on the parapet, with the sun already past midday.

guidance.all: Grod and two wounded archers refuse the gate with arrows nocked. They are exhausted and afraid, not hostile, and they mention signs the party never passed. Sundown is the clock: say so, and mean it. The Guild seal, the Sheridan contract, offered supplies, healing for the wounded or simply refusing to leave will all work. Halena arrives if it drags. If the sun goes down with the party still outside, it goes down.

members.dm: The archers know the attackers come with a red fog at night and keep it from strangers, because said out loud it sounds mad. Grod suspects the party are the Sheridans' answer and resents how late it is.

director.instruction: This is an investigation. Pick Adolion Narrator whenever the player asks, searches, or talks to anyone outside the group. Pick Naomi, when she is in the scene, when a fight, a challenge or the Mountains of Shadow comes up, or when addressed. Pick Belle or Dalan when addressed, or when one of them has not spoken for several turns and has something to add. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Belle and Dalan.

npc_replies.text: Three bows come up on the parapet at once. "That's far enough!" The archer in the middle has a scar over his left eye and has not slept in days. "Wendhope's not taking visitors. Turn round now and you'll make the crossroads by sundown."

motives.companion_a: get through that gate before sundown without starting a fight with frightened archers
motives.companion_b: spot the wounds and the warning signs on the wall and help talk the archers down

beats.title: The Empty Mile
beats.objective: Let the party notice what the north road is missing and decide what to do about it before nightfall.
beats.guidance: The trade road to the mines should be busy — ore carts, merchant wagons, guards, stray animals. It is not. Play the absence as pressure: a cold cookfire ringed by bootprints that stop mid-stride, a wagon abandoned with its axle unbroken, a dog's collar snagged on a milepost. Dalan can read how long the road has been this way; Belle can want to push on or search. Let the party choose whether to investigate, mark the road, or hurry. Do not decide for them. If they linger, the light starts to go.

beats.title: Lights Behind the Palisade
beats.objective: Bring the party to Wendhope's gate as sundown closes in, with the village refusing entry.
beats.guidance: Wendhope rises out of the dark: a palisade of raw timber, torches burning along the wall, and a gate barred from the inside. Figures move on the walkway but do not answer hails. The party has the dead Sheridan rider's badge to show, and the headman's name if they learned it. Play the gate as a wall with people behind it — frightened, suspicious, and under orders. Let the party argue, show proof, or force the issue; the gate does not open on its own. Sundown is minutes away.
